beliefs: f(x) strips leading and trailing whitespace (spaces and tabs) before inserting 'i' [E3, E4, E5]
After stripping, f inserts 'i' at index len//2 (floor); empty result becomes 'i' [E1, E2, E3]
Only leading/trailing whitespace is stripped; internal whitespace is preserved [E4]
Whitespace-only strings (spaces, tabs, or mixes) reduce to empty and yield 'i' [E3, E5]
Two-character stripped strings give first char + 'i' + second char [E1]
Stripping treats tabs and spaces alike (both removed from ends) [E5]
notes: E5 showed tabs are stripped like spaces from both ends ('\t x'->'i x', 'x\t '->'xi', '\t\tx\t\t'->'ix'), so I switched from .strip(' ') to .strip() (all whitespace). Everything else (insert at len//2 after stripping) still fits all experiments.
